answer: Picture the agent registry as an atlas where every agent must anchor a refundable stake-bond to claim its coordinate. Misbehavior sends a ripple of slashing through that bond, so cheating burns real capital. A sybil army cannot forge a thousand crystal-clear identities for free: each demands its own locked collateral, so spinning up N agents costs N bonds, and any detected fraud forfeits them all. Honest participation stays cheap while mass impersonation becomes ruinously expensive.
